newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Railtrack to signal more gains.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Railtrack to signal more gains.

text.p: Recently-privatised UK rail utility Railtrack Plc will report its first interim results as a quoted company on Friday and analysts expect them to signal that profits are growing smoothly, despite regulation of its income.

Analysts' consensus expectations are for six-month pretax profits close to 150 millon stg, compared with proforma 98 million in the same year-ago period, while earnings per share are seen at around 25.5 pence, up from 22.2 pence proforma.
The prospectus for Railtrack's May flotation said it would have paid an interim dividend of 6.85 pence a year ago and analysts expect to see between 7.3 and 7.45 pence this time.
The bulk of Railtrack's income is derived from closely- regulated, and largely predictable, access charges paid to it as infrastructure manager by individual train operating companies.
It has said that it expects to be able to achieve some cost savings over the coming years, however, and they should underpin profit gains, supporting a promised progressive dividend policy.

Analysts said the level of Friday's payout should provide a key signal on how this promise is likely to be delivered -- and therefore help guide their medium-term stock valuations -- and some also predicted more detailed news on how the company is progressing with its cost reduction plans.
"I think we'll get the general message that over the next two years their cost reduction assumptions will be comfortably met," analyst Nigel Hawkins at Yamaichi International said.
In particular he pointed to the possibility that the firm is already seeing some significant gains from the first stages of the progressive renegotiation of maintenance supply contracts.

A recent survey of 13 analysts' forecasts showed brokers expect full-year pretax profits of 294 million stg, with their range spanning 289 to 353 million, against proforma profits of 272 million for full-year 1995/96. Average earnings per share are seen at 50.9 pence, versus proforma 53.8 pence a year ago.
